correctness.rationale: The reconstructed payoff differences yield the stated field x(1−x)(2x−1)[a+(b−a)x]. Differentiation at the three permanent equilibria gives −a, −b, and (a+b)/4, so the three lines and the frozen intersection are exhaustive. In the signed attracting endpoint basins, substitution u=x or 1−x gives u̇=−cu²(1−u)(1−2u); z=1/u yields ż=c(z−1)(z−2)/z² and antiderivative F′=z²/[(z−1)(z−2)], so F(z)=ct+F(z0). The expansion F(z)=z+3log z+O(1/z) proves 1/u=ct−3log(ct)+F(z0)+o(1). At the attracting interior branch a+b=0, u=|x−1/2| satisfies u̇=−cu²(1−4u²); G′=z²/(z²−4), G(z)=z+O(1/z), giving 1/u=ct+G(z0)+o(1). Scalar monotonicity proves convergence without finite-time collision; the opposite basins and frozen case are explicitly excluded. The packaged standalone code passes 12,859 checks; finite checks do not prove the infinite-time statements.

value.rationale: At the three natural payoff-collision hypersurfaces identified in the motivating model, linear stability becomes silent about convergence speed. The exact phase-dependent implicit laws and the nonzero endpoint −3log(ct) correction versus its exact cancellation for the interior collision permit distinct measurable critical transients and show why analogous nonhyperbolic equilibria have different finite-time behavior. It closes all critical one-sided regimes of the model (including the source’s degenerate S=P case) and furnishes testable quantitative critical signatures. The contribution is a natural complete boundary classification, not a claimed new general ODE integration method.
